title: Grade 12 Chemistry — p-Block Elements
description: Group 15–18 elements — nitrogen family, oxygen family, halogens, noble gases (CBSE Ch. 7)
subject: chemistry

questions.question: Group 15 elements (Nitrogen family) in order are:
questions.explanation: Group 15 (VA): N (Nitrogen), P (Phosphorus), As (Arsenic), Sb (Antimony), Bi (Bismuth). Their general valence configuration is ns²np³, giving them 5 valence electrons and common oxidation states of +3, +5, and −3.

questions.question: The general electronic configuration of Group 15 elements is:
questions.explanation: Group 15 (VA) elements have ns²np³ valence configuration — 2 electrons in the s-subshell and 3 electrons in the p-subshell. The half-filled p³ configuration (one electron per orbital) gives them extra stability.

questions.question: Group 16 elements are called Chalcogens. They are:
questions.explanation: Group 16 (VIA) — Chalcogens: O (Oxygen), S (Sulphur), Se (Selenium), Te (Tellurium), Po (Polonium). 'Chalcogen' comes from Greek 'chalcos' (ore/copper) + 'gen' (producer). Many metal ores are oxides or sulphides.

questions.question: Water (H₂O) is a liquid at room temperature while H₂S is a gas. This is because:
options: Oxygen has a higher atomic mass than sulphur
H₂O has a much higher boiling point due to strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding
H₂S has stronger covalent bonds than H₂O
H₂O molecules are larger and heavier
questions.explanation: H₂O forms extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds (O–H···O) due to the high electronegativity and small size of oxygen. This dramatically raises the boiling point (100°C vs −60°C for H₂S). H₂S cannot form significant hydrogen bonds (S is larger, less electronegative).

questions.question: NH₃ (ammonia) has a pyramidal geometry because:
options: N has no lone pairs — all electrons form bonds
N has one lone pair of electrons that occupy one of the four sp³ hybrid orbitals, creating a pyramidal shape
N has two lone pairs pushing the bonds into a square planar arrangement
NH₃ is a linear molecule with bond angle 180°
questions.explanation: N in NH₃ is sp³ hybridised with 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair. The lone pair repels bonding pairs more strongly, compressing the H–N–H bond angle to 107° (less than 109.5°). The shape is trigonal pyramidal (VSEPR theory).

questions.question: PCl₅ (phosphorus pentachloride) has which molecular geometry?
questions.explanation: PCl₅ has 5 bond pairs and no lone pairs. P uses d-orbitals (unlike N which cannot) to accommodate 5 bonds — sp³d hybridisation. The geometry is trigonal bipyramidal with 3 equatorial Cl at 120° and 2 axial Cl at 90°.

questions.question: Group 17 elements are called Halogens. Which of the following is the most electronegative element?
questions.explanation: Fluorine (F) is the most electronegative element in the periodic table (Pauling scale: 4.0). It has the smallest atomic radius in Group 17, and its electrons are closest to the nucleus — creating the strongest pull on bonding electrons.

questions.question: Fluorine cannot form oxyacids unlike other halogens (Cl, Br, I). The reason is:
options: Fluorine reacts violently with oxygen, preventing oxyacid formation
Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen, so it cannot donate electrons to oxygen
Fluorine has no d-orbitals in its valence shell (2nd period) and cannot expand its octet beyond 8 electrons
Fluorine is a gas and cannot form acidic compounds
questions.explanation: Fluorine is in the 2nd period — its valence shell (n=2) has no d-orbitals. It cannot expand its octet, limiting it to a maximum covalency of 1. Heavier halogens (Cl, Br, I) use empty d-orbitals to form multiple bonds with O, creating oxyacids (HClO, HClO₂, HClO₃, HClO₄).

questions.question: Group 18 elements (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn) are called noble gases because they are generally:
options: The most reactive elements — they react with almost everything
Found only in noble metal ores
Chemically inert — they have completely filled valence shells (stable octet/duplet)
The heaviest elements in their respective periods
questions.explanation: Noble gases have fully filled valence shells (He: 1s², others: ns²np⁶). This gives them maximum stability — no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons. They exist as monoatomic gases and rarely form compounds.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds of Xenon (Xe) is NOT known to exist?
questions.explanation: Xenon forms XeF₂, XeF₄, and XeF₆ (and some oxide compounds). XeF₈ does not exist — Xe can accommodate at most 6 bonds using its 5d orbitals and available electrons. XeF₆ is already the highest known xenon fluoride.

questions.question: The geometry of XeF₄ is square planar because it has:
options: 4 bond pairs and no lone pairs
4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs in opposite axial positions
questions.explanation: Xe in XeF₄ has 4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs = 6 electron pairs (sp³d² hybridisation). The 2 lone pairs occupy the axial positions (180° apart), and the 4 F atoms are in the equatorial plane — giving square planar geometry.

questions.question: Interhalogen compounds are formed when:
options: A halogen reacts with a noble gas
Two halogen elements combine with each other (e.g., ClF, BrF₃, IF₇)
A halogen reacts with oxygen to form an oxyhalide
questions.explanation: Interhalogens are compounds formed between two different halogen elements (e.g., ClF, ClF₃, BrF₃, BrF₅, IF₅, IF₇). The heavier/larger halogen is the central atom. They are generally more reactive than their parent halogens.

questions.question: The most stable allotrope of sulphur at room temperature is:
questions.explanation: Rhombic sulphur (α-sulphur) is the most stable allotrope at room temperature (up to 95.6°C — the transition point). Above 95.6°C, monoclinic sulphur (β-sulphur) becomes stable. Both forms consist of S₈ puckered ring molecules.

questions.question: The bond angle in H₂S is about 92°, which is less than the bond angle in H₂O (≈104.5°). This is because:
options: S is more electronegative than O, pulling bonds closer together
H₂S has more lone pairs than H₂O
S is larger than O — the S–H bonding orbitals are farther apart, and lone pair repulsion is less effective at compressing the bond angle
H₂O has only one lone pair while H₂S has two
questions.explanation: Both H₂O and H₂S have 2 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs. In H₂O, O uses sp³ hybrid orbitals (strong lone pair–bond pair repulsion → 104.5°). In H₂S, S is larger — bonding uses mostly p-orbitals (90° natural angle). Weaker lone-pair compression gives ≈92°.

questions.question: The maximum covalency shown by nitrogen (N) is 4. Which statement explains why N cannot show a covalency of 5 like phosphorus?
options: Nitrogen has only 5 electrons and cannot share more than 4
Nitrogen has no d-orbitals in its valence shell (n = 2), so it cannot expand its octet beyond 8 electrons
Nitrogen is too electronegative to form more than 4 bonds
Nitrogen's atomic mass is too small to accommodate 5 bonds
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is in the 2nd period — its valence shell (n=2) has only s and p subshells (no d-orbitals). Maximum 4 pairs = 8 electrons fill the valence shell. Phosphorus (3rd period, has 3d orbitals) can accommodate up to 5 or 6 bonds using these empty d-orbitals.
